top.title: Virginia Tech basketball: Hokies lose first game to Oklahoma State after terrible second half
top.description: SIOUX CITY, IOWA - NOVEMBER 10: Ben Hammond #3 of the Virginia Tech Hokies drives against Isaia Howard #23 of the Iowa Hawkeyes during the first half at Tyson Events Center on November 10, 2026 in Sioux City, Iowa. (Photo by Steven Branscombe/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 6-0 Virginia Tech Hokies were back Sunday in the Shriners Children’s Charleston Classic in Charleston, South Carolina. The opponent: the Oklahoma State Cowboys. After a back-and-forth first half with the lead changing often, the Cowboys took control in the second half, outscoring the Hokies 65-39 in the final 20 minutes to win 106-80. Remarkably, this game was tied at halftime. Both teams were hot from the field, with OSU shooting 59% and the Hokies 47% in the first half. Tech made 8-of-15 (53%) from beyond the arc in the first half, while the Cowboys made 5-of-10. While the Hokies cooled off in the second half, Oklahoma State only got hotter. VT made only 11 of 28 field-goal attempts in the second half, including 4-for-14 from the 3-point line, while the Cowboys shot an unheard-of 74% in the second half. And there you have it, that’s the game. The back-and-forth action from the first half carried into the second half. However, back-to-back buckets from Ben Hammond and Amani Hansberry at the 16:31 mark gave the Hokies a 54-51 lead. The crowd sensed the tide might be turning in Virginia Tech’s favor. Instead, it spurred a run by the Cowboys that opened up the game. Oklahoma State scored the next 11 points to build an 8-point lead. The Cowboys never looked back. After a Hammond 3-pointer and two Jaylen Curry free throws cut the lead back to 64-59, OSU scored 13 in a row to blow it wide open. Virginia Tech finishes the weekend 1-1 in Charleston, suffering its first loss of the season. Next up for Virginia Tech is a date with Old Dominion at Cassell Coliseum on Friday. Hammond led the Hokies with 24 points and five rebounds. He was phenomenal as usual, but he had little help. Curry scored 18, but in playing against his former team, he let his emotions get the best of him early, starting down Oklahoma State coach Steve Lutz. Mike Young and Lutz quickly went head-to-head, but it ended as fast as it began, and both coaches laughed it off. Curry led the Hokies with 7 assists, but exhibited poor shot selection at times. Hansberry had a rough game, finishing with 9 points and 6 rebounds and making only 3-of-10 from the field. OSU outrebounded the Hokies 33-27 and Tech had 11 turnovers. Virginia Tech’s continued insistence on living by the 3-point shot can sometimes haunt them. It did on Sunday. Plus, when another team shoots 74% in a half, it’s hard to beat them. The good news is that rarely happens.

Before a single snap was played, though, the crowd made sure that the night would be remembered for more than just football. As Mexican singer Majo Aguilar performed the Mexican national anthem, the entire stadium sang along with her in a moment that quickly went viral. Fans and media members alike were blown away, with many saying it gave them chills. ‘A MUST LISTEN’ The NFL announced back in September that Aguilar would sing the Mexican national anthem, while Oakland-born singer-songwriter MXKA would perform the U.S. national anthem. Aguilar, a member of Mexico’s famed Aguilar music family and a cousin of Ángela Aguilar, has more than 533 million global streams and also sang the anthem as part of Telemundo’s World Cup coverage. “I feel very happy to be able to perform the Mexican National Anthem. Mexico is a beautiful country with a rich culture,” Aguilar said in the NFL’s announcement . “Thank you to the NFL for inviting me to be part of such a special moment and allowing me to represent my country. It fills me with pride to be Mexican.” Needless to say, she and the crowd delivered. Video of the performance shared by SportsCenter racked up more than 500,000 views within a couple of hours, and plenty of people chimed in with their reactions. top.title: Jaguars defense tougher as game wore on, but didn't get the stop it needed
top.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars defense played well enough to win on Nov. 22 against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium Even Jaguars coach Liam Coen , whose offense simply wasn't up to the task, admitted as much after the Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the Giants . "They gave us plenty of opportunities," Coen said about his defense. "We didn't play complementary football. We turned it over, they scored points. We get turnovers, we didn't score points. I felt like you hold a team to 23 points in the National Football League, you should win some of those games." But not this one. There were some heartening aspects about how the Jags played defense against the Giants. Edge rusher Josh Hines-Allen got his first solo sack since opening week, forced a fumble and batted down a pass. Safety Antonio Johnson had a big fumble return and came an eyelash away from an interception on the Giants' next offensive play. New additions Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux on the defensive line helped the Jags hold New York running backs to 2.6 yards per carry and the Giants had only 77 yards rushing, nearly half on scrambles by quarterback J.J. McCarthy. The Jaguars defense played especially well during a dominating sequence of four second-half possessions in a row in which McCarthy and his two key weapons, running back Cam Skattebo and wide receiver Malik Nabers, were simply squashed. Jags defense produced opportunities for offense New York moved the ball on its first two possessions of the second half, but Dominic Zvada hooked a 32-yard field goal attempt, and Johnson scooped up a fumble forced by Hines-Allen and returned it 42 yards to the Giants' 31 after McCarthy had moved his offense to the Jags' 32. The Jaguars offense failed to take advantage of either opportunity. They had to punt after the missed field goal and Trevor Lawrence threw an incomplete pass on fourth-and-one at the New York 11 following Johnson's turnover. The defense only redoubled their efforts after that. On New York's next four possessions, McCarthy was 1 of 11, and his completion went for only 8 yards. The Giants had 11 total yards on those possessions. The Giants also beat themselves, including a holding penalty on guard Francis Mauigoa nullifying McCarthy's 29-yard scramble. The biggest self-inflicted wound came after an 8-yard pass to Nabers. Travis Hunter made the tackle but was hit late by center Ben Hudson, drawing an unnecessary roughness flag. Instead of second-and-two, the dead-ball penalty made it third-and-17 and safety Jessie Bates III blitzed to force McCarthy into an completion. Aside from that, it was all Jaguars. New York didn't get a first down on those possessions and got three points on one, Zvada's 43-yard field goal, thanks to the Jaguars' offense: Lawrence was intercepted for the second time, and Paulson Abedo returned it to the Jags' 28. top.title: Gene Steratore questions review process in Giants-Jaguars
top.description: Credit: NBC, CBS The New York Giants upset the Jacksonville Jaguars in one of the most stunning results of the NFL’s Week 11 Sunday slate. After carrying a 20–6 lead into the fourth quarter, the Giants were able to hold off a late charge from the Jaguars and secure the win at home by a score of 23–18. But it’s possible the game could have had a different outcome had one close call gone in the Jaguars’ favor. The call in question came with 12 minutes left to play and the Jaguars driving in Giants territory. Facing third-and-9, Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw a dart to receiver Parker Washington, who appeared to come down with the ball right on the line in the back of the end zone, but the play was ruled an incompletion on the field. The Jaguars challenged the incomplete call, and as the broadcast watched the replays in slow motion, it seemed pretty clear that Washington caught the ball, controlled it, and got two feet in bounds for the score. “At this point, when Parker Washington after the bobble possesses that football, I still had the right foot down as he’s falling, then I have the left foot touch,” rules analyst Gene Steratore told the broadcast booth. “I see the ball move a little bit, but I did not think that he lost possession of the football. You can clearly see at this point, I have possession, right foot down, tap with the left foot. Yes, does the ball move a little, but the right hand in my opinion continues to keep that secure enough that I would say in my opinion, that is a ball movement, but he is still controlling that football. I think it’s a touchdown.” But the people that control the replay reviews didn’t agree with Steratore, and the call of incomplete that was made on the field stood. The Jaguars would settle for a field goal, cutting the lead to 20–9. “I did not think he lost possession of the football… I think it’s a touchdown, fellas.” CBS rules analyst Gene Steratore disagreed with this being ruled incomplete after review on a potential Parker Washington TD for the Jaguars. https://t.co/4RdlPYAYXQ — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 23, 2026 Later on in the broadcast, Steratore reported on the conversation he had with the league office explaining the reasoning behind the decision. “They felt like there was not enough clear and obvious evidence to change the ruling on the field, which was an incomplete pass. top.title: Texas Football Could Deliver a Major SEC Championship Statement Before Alabama Even Takes the Field
top.description: Oct 17, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns Head Coach Steve Sarkisian during the first half against the Florida Gators at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) COLLEGE STATION, Texas — Texas has an opportunity to make the Southeastern Conference’s championship race considerably less complicated before Saturday’s games even begin. The Longhorns visit Texas A&M on Friday, Nov. 27, with a potential trip to Atlanta hanging in the balance. Meanwhile, Alabama and Tennessee must wait until Saturday to complete their conference schedules. That timing could prove important. If the right results fall into place Friday, Texas could secure the second SEC Championship Game berth before either of its competitors takes the field. Texas has an opportunity to seize control Texas (9-2, 6-2 SEC) enters Rivalry Week tied with Alabama and Tennessee for second place. Georgia has already secured the conference’s first championship game berth. However, Texas holds several favorable tiebreaking advantages. The Longhorns defeated Tennessee 20-17 earlier this season. Additionally, Texas holds an advantage over Alabama based on results against common SEC opponents. Those results provide Texas with a favorable path if the conference race produces a two-team tie. The Egg Bowl could play an unexpected role Texas’ championship hopes also depend on the outcome of a rivalry game involving two other SEC programs. Ole Miss hosts Mississippi State at noon Friday, several hours before Texas visits Texas A&M. If Ole Miss defeats Mississippi State and Texas subsequently beats the Aggies, the Longhorns would clinch a championship game berth regardless of Saturday’s results. That scenario involves the SEC’s opponents’ winning percentage tiebreaker. Consequently, a game in Oxford could help determine whether Texas plays for a conference championship in Atlanta. Texas A&M has plenty of motivation Texas A&M (4-7, 1-7 SEC) enters the matchup with a disappointing conference record. However, the Aggies have an opportunity to deny their biggest rival a potential championship appearance. That possibility adds another layer to an already emotional rivalry. A Texas victory would improve the Longhorns to 10-2 and strengthen their College Football Playoff résumé. Meanwhile, a loss would eliminate Texas from the SEC Championship Game race. For Steve Sarkisian’s program, Friday represents an opportunity to finish the regular season with a statement. For Texas A&M, it represents an opportunity to make sure its rival does not get that satisfaction. And depending on what happens earlier in Oxford, the Longhorns might enter Kyle Field knowing exactly what a victory would mean. top.title: Eric Garcia reveals Hansi Flick’s half-time message to Barcelona after comeback win over Villarreal
top.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 22: Eric Garcia of FC Barcelona celebrates his team's third goal, scored by an own goal by Pau Navarro (not in frame) of Villarreal CF, during the LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 match between FC Barcelona and Villarreal CF at Spotify Camp Nou on November 22, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo by Pablo Rodriguez/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images) | Getty Images Eric Garcia revealed Hansi Flick’s message to his players after Barcelona came from 2-0 down to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday in an eventful game. Two early goals put the visitors in charge of the match, while a missed penalty from Lamine Yamal made it feel like it simply wasn’t going to be Barca’s day. However, the champions turned it around in the second half, with Eric asked afterwards what Flick had said to his players at the break. “He told us to respect our positions and to stick to our roles. We knew that once we scored a goal, it would be very difficult to stop us,” he said. “We scored the first one, the second came almost immediately, and with our fans pushing us on at the Camp Nou, we had even more energy.” Garcia also highlighted the importance of the victory that keeps Barcelona top of the table. “It has enormous importance. Villarreal is an excellent team, and this was a complicated match after the international break, especially with the wind. Sometimes you take these matches for granted, thinking you’ll win them easily. But today reminded us that nothing is guaranteed. Every match has to be fought for from the first minute,” he added. “Villarreal is a Champions League-level team with a fantastic coach. They had two chances and scored two goals. But after that, we woke up, started playing our game, and they barely threatened us again. In the second half, we played the way we should always play.”

top.title: Ravens Report Card, Week 11: Mistakes and miscues mount in sixth straight loss
top.description: Nov 22, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Carolina Panthers linebacker Devin Lloyd (55) tackles Baltimore Ravens cornerback Nate Wiggins (2) during the fourth quarter at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens dropped their fifth consecutive game on Monday night, losing to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers by three points (23-20). Here are report card grades for the team’s position groups from another disheartening defeat in Week 10. Quarterback: C+ Jacoby Brissett made a number of good throws in this game and orchestrated five scoring drives. It was not his fault that the Ravens fumbled the ball multiple times and his pass-catchers dropped more than five passes. The veteran finished with a 24-of-37 passing line with 276 yards through the air. His touchdown pass came via a trick play to a wide-open Rashod Bateman for a 25-yard strike in the fourth quarter. Brissett was not perfect, however. He was inaccurate on some pass attempts and threw a game-sealing interception on the team’s final drive, which was an inexcusable mistake where he should have thrown the ball away. The Ravens may not have ultimately gotten down the field into position for a game-winning field goal, but there was time left to do so and Brissett’s interception cost them that opportunity. Running Back: C- It’s difficult to give a poor grade to the running backs when Derrick Henry and Justice Hill combined for 163 rushing yards, averaged over nine yards per carry and scored two combined touchdowns. However, while both were effective churning out yards on the ground, they also each lost a fumble. Hill’s fumble at the goal line negated a would-be long touchdown run in the first half that instead resulted in a touchback. Then, in the fourth quarter with the Ravens trailing by six points, Henry had the ball poked out after making a screen catch. It was a controversial call that maybe should have been ruled an incompletion, but nevertheless Henry’s ball security needs to be better. Fortunately, the Panthers did not score points off either of these turnovers — but they still costed the Ravens valuable points and possessions. Wide Receiver: C + Zay Flowers had his most productive performance in several weeks, reeling in a team-high eight receptions on 11 targets for 97 yards. He was open a lot and created yards in space on crossing routes, which has been Flowers’ bread and butter this season. He did have one drop just before halftime that would have been a long gain. Rashod Bateman started hot with 67 yards and a long touchdown catch early in the game, but only finished with two catches on six targets. Devontez Walker had a nice 34-yard grab on his only target. It was a quiet outing for Ja’Kobi Lane who was not credited with a target after receiving the most throws his way of anyone last week. top.title: ‘It just can’t happen’- Pat Freiermuth calls out DK Metcalf after Steelers ejection
top.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth has delivered an honest verdict on DK Metcalf’s ejection against the Philadelphia Eagles, admitting his teammate’s actions were unacceptable. Metcalf was sent off during the third quarter of Pittsburgh’s 19-16 defeat after receiving his second personal foul penalty of the game for poking Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean in the eye. The incident quickly became one of the biggest talking points following the Steelers’ narrow loss, with Freiermuth making it clear that he supports his close friend but expects better from him. Pat Freiermuth sends clear message to DK Metcalf after Pittsburgh Steelers ejection Speaking to reporters after the game, Freiermuth did not attempt to defend Metcalf’s actions, despite their close relationship in Pittsburgh. “He knows that’s unacceptable,” Freiermuth said. “He’ll be fine. But like I said, he’s one of my closest friends on the team, and he knows I have his back in those situations. But it just can’t happen.” The comments offered a glimpse into how Metcalf’s behaviour was viewed inside the Steelers locker room, with Freiermuth making it clear that friendship does not excuse what happened. Metcalf’s ejection also came during another frustrating outing for the wide receiver, who managed just one reception for two yards from four targets before being sent off. The two-time Pro Bowler has struggled to find consistency this season. He has not recorded more than two receptions in a game since his 11-catch, 93-yard performance against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Across 10 games, Metcalf has recorded 36 receptions for 434 yards and two touchdowns from 74 targets. That represents a drop from his first season in Pittsburgh, when he finished with 59 catches for 850 yards and six touchdowns across 15 games. Metcalf had already faced disciplinary trouble last season after being suspended following an altercation with a Detroit Lions fan. With Pittsburgh now 6-4 following the defeat to Philadelphia, the Steelers will need their leading receiver to find his form while avoiding further incidents. Freiermuth’s message was clear: Metcalf has the support of his teammates, but another costly moment is something the team cannot afford. top.title: 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz carted off the field in Mexico City game vs. Vikings
top.description: San Francisco 49ers offensive tackle Colton McKivitz (68) is carted off the field after an injury during the first half of an NFL football game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. (AP Photo/Eduardo Verdugo) (Eduardo Verdugo/AP Photo/Eduardo Verdugo) MEXICO CITY - San Francisco 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome injury to his lower left leg in the second quarter of their meeting with the Vikings on Sunday night and was carted off the field at Estadio Banorte with an air cast. McKivitz, 30, was bent backward when running back Christian McCaffrey was tackled into him at the end of a 4-yard run. McKivitz rolled over and emerged from the pile with his lower left leg bent at an awkward angle. Left tackle Trent Williams slammed his helmet to the turf and players from both teams quickly took a knee, many looking away from McKivitz, as the 49ers' medical staff raced onto the field. Williams embraced McKivitz before he was carted away as most of the team's roster was on the field to show their support. McKivitz has been among the most durable players on a team known for its chronic injury issues and was in the midst of the best season of his seven-year career. Since becoming a full-time starter in 2023, McKivitz has made 62 consecutive starts, and he entered Sunday's game without allowing a sack in 327 pass-blocking snaps this season. The 49ers signed McKivitz to a three-year, $45 million contract extension before last year's season opener. McKivitz was replaced Sunday by Vederian Lowe, 27, a five-year veteran with 25 career starts. The 49ers signed Lowe to a two-year, $9.25 million contract in March. top.title: Greenwich girls swimming holds off Ridgefield for second straight State Open title
top.description: Greenwich poses for a team photo with their championship plaque and banner after winning the CIAC State Open girls swimming and diving championship on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, at Yale. (Kevin Roberts/Hearst Connecticut Media) NEW HAVEN - The Greenwich girls swimming and diving team captured its second straight State Open title and 23rd overall Sunday by holding off second-place Ridgefield 634-617.5 at Yale. The Cardinals, under first-year head coach Megan Kelly , lost to the Tigers in the regular season before beating them by 18.5 points at FCIACs and 45.5 at Class LL. They completed the trifecta at the Open. "I'm so proud of them," said Kelly, who took over for Brendan Heller, who won four Class LL championships, three State Open titles and three FCIAC championships in five seasons as coach. "Coming in, we knew we had a lot of work to get where we were last year, which was winning the Triple Crown (conference, class and Open titles). It was really tough at the beginning of the season … but they worked really hard in the pool." The Open title was the Cardinals' fourth in the last six years. Ridgefield won crowns in 2022 and 2024. Greenwich senior Kensington Worden led the way with a dramatic victory in the 50 freestyle, touching the wall in 23.57, only .03 seconds ahead of the second-place finisher. For Worden, it was a dream come true. "Coming in as a freshman at this program, it is beyond my wildest dreams ever to become an Open champion," Worden said. "I'm just so happy." Senior Ellison Charette gave Greenwich its second individual title of the meet with a time of 4:57.33 in the 500 freestyle. After that, it was the Cardinals' depth that held off Ridgefield, which had two wins from Zsofia Milak (50.55 in 100 free and 1:50.58 in 200 free) and two from its relays (200 free and 400 free). Ridgefield's 200 free relay of Milak, Dalia Katra, Mary Kelly and Ellen Griffin broke the Open record with a time of 1:34.18. The Tigers held the previous record of 1:35.48, set in 2022. The foursome also won the 400 free relay to end the night. On Thursday, Cardinals sophomore Alden Charette defended her diving crown with a record 561.55 points. The Cardinals' game plan for Sunday was simple. "I told them before this meet, if everyone just moves up one spot individually, we can win," said coach Kelly, a Greenwich alumna and former All-American swimmer. Mission accomplished, but not without months of hard work. "It might seem like it's tiring going two and a half hours every single day, but we are all there and all doing it together, which makes it more special. ... It's full of support and love and everything in between," Worden said. Other individual winners included Norwalk/Brien McMahon's Emma Giafardino in the 200 IM (2:05.05), Weston's McKenzie Parsons in the 100 butterfly (55.54), Wilton's Vedha Kongettira in the 100 backstroke (56.45) and Brookfield's Maggie O'Hara in the 100 breaststroke (1:04.36). top.description: BERKELEY, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 21: Stanford Cardinal players celebrates with the Stanford Axe after they defeated the California Golden Bears 44-28 in the 129th Big Game at California Memorial Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Berkeley, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Notre Dame’s 2026 college football schedule has been called many thing over the last eight months, but “tough” or anywhere near the word “hard” was certainly not among them. Still, some have mentioned that this Irish schedule could look a lot trickier as the season progresses. While they may eventually be true, it may not matter all that much (except for message boards and social media). Notre Dame took a minute or two to get going against the Wisconsin Badgers in the season opener, but eventually the Irish whooped them 42-13. Notre Dame welcomed the Rice Owls to South Bend for the home opener, and sent them back to Texas with a 52-0 loss. Although the Irish were big favorites against Michigan State, they got their best shot — and still beat the Spartans 27-10. The Irish were once again massive favorites over a Big 10 team, and they more than covered against Purdue with a 49-10 win that was never that close. Notre Dame was better than a three touchdown favorite against North Carolina, but ran into a bit of a clunker (and rain) and beat the Tar Heels 37-26. After two weeks on the road, Notre Dame returned to South Bend and the homecooking did them well as the Irish destroyed the Stanford Cardinal 58-7. Disaster hit the Irish against BYU in a 28-24 loss, and no matter what part of the game you want to complain about (because there was quite a bit) the simplest thing to say is that Notre Dame flat out got outplayed by the Cougars. Against Navy, Notre Dame took a slower path than fans would like, but in the end the Irish won the game 35-13 and completely shutdown the Middies in the 2nd half. Notre Dame did “the thing” that fans and pundits have been waiting on, and took down No. 1 Miami in South Bend 31-24. There was no hangover from the massive win over the Canes, and the Irish whipped Boston College at home, 41-7. Notre Dame took care of business against SMU in what was kind of a weird game, but still dominating on many levels. Next up for the Irish is a trip to Syracuse for the final game of the regular season. Notre Dame is still likely to be favored in every game this season, and they are still a popular pick to win the national championship. Their strength of schedule probably isn’t going to matter much, but let’s keep track of it anyway. Gas supply to power plants increased by 10 per cent to 0.571 bcf/d in October. Deliveries to gas-based industries also rose, while supplies to commercial users declined. Domestic supply increased by 2.3 per cent to 2.113 bcf/d, while deliveries to NLNG grew by three per cent to 2.838 bcf/d. Gas supply to power plants increased by 10 per cent to 0.571 bcf/d in October. Deliveries to gas-based industries also rose, while supplies to commercial users declined. nigeria.title: Ajaokuta: NES blames collapse of long-term planning for 40-year stalemate
nigeria.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The President, Nigerian Economic Society (NES), Dr. Baba Musa, has blamed the collapse of long-term economic planning for the failure of the Ajaokuta Steel Company to become operational more than four decades after its establishment. Musa, who spoke at the National Growth & Development Forum (NGDF) 2026 in Abuja, said Nigeria lost the link between economic planning and execution, resulting in the abandonment or underperformance of strategic national projects. “History demands candour. Somewhere along the way, we lost vital links between plan and performance. We built, but did not always maintain,” he said. According to him, the oil windfall of the 1970s diverted the country from agriculture and non-oil exports which had previously sustained the economy. “The oil windfall of the 1970s drew us away from the agriculture and non-oil exports that had sustained us. Strategic projects such as the Ajaokuta Steel Complex, begun with great promise, have yet to fulfil it four decades on. “And when formal planning gave way in the mid-1980s, long-term strategy too often yielded to visions that changed with administrations,” Musa said. He said Nigeria must learn from its past policy failures to avoid repeating mistakes that have undermined economic development. “The Nigeria we want must be built upon the Nigeria we have, and the Nigeria we have,” he added. The NES president also expressed concern that economic reforms had yet to translate into shared prosperity, noting that about 63 per cent of Nigerians, estimated at 140 million people, lived below the poverty line in 2025, according to the World Bank. “Macroeconomic stability is necessary, but it is not yet shared prosperity. A stable exchange rate is not yet a full dinner table. Stability is the foundation; it is not the building,” he said. Musa called for an economy that generates jobs, supports the poor, boosts domestic production, invests in human capital and promotes disciplined public finance and credible institutions. Similarly, President, Capital Market Academics of Nigeria, Prof. Uche Uwaleke, said economic reforms must be measured by their impact on citizens’ welfare, job creation, purchasing power and poverty reduction. nigeria.title: Climate talks collapse in chaotic end to COP31
nigeria.description: Climate advocates reacted with indignation on Monday to the COP31 summit ending in failure, with contentious talks collapsing over fossil fuels after the meeting in Turkey stretched into record overtime. The final agreement was rejected on Sunday in a chaotic finale to the UN climate summit that ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who urged nations to send fossil fuels “the way of the dinosaurs” during a fiery appearance at the talks, expressed deep dismay. “I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands,” the outgoing UN chief said in a statement. COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines”. “Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision… And that’s disappointing. Very disappointing,” Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, told a throng of reporters. More than 49 hours after the summit was supposed to end, COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum banged the gavel to conclude the marathon talks. Calls for reform Bowen said the summit backdrop was “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory”, as soaring energy prices and fallout from the Middle East war complicated the search for unity. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, whose country co-hosted the summit with Turkey, attributed the failure of the talks to “difficult geopolitical times”. Under pressure to show progress in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal, Bowen sought an overarching “cover decision” to prove countries were still united in tackling the crisis. But his plan unravelled as familiar fault lines emerged over fossil fuels, with the EU and Saudi Arabia locking horns over the pace of the shift away from coal, oil and gas. Onuigbo described parliamentary action as central to bridging the gap between international climate negotiations and domestic implementation. He stressed that legislators must ensure that agreements reached at COP meetings were reflected in national laws, budgetary allocations and effective government oversight. nigeria.title: Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29
nigeria.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. Diri explained that the final casualty figure had yet to be established as efforts were still ongoing to recover the affected vessel. ﻿ He, however, said some passengers might still be trapped inside the boat. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, adding that the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. The boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways, according to a preliminary police report. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings. entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? sports.title: Virginia Tech basketball: Hokies lose first game to Oklahoma State after terrible second half
sports.description: SIOUX CITY, IOWA - NOVEMBER 10: Ben Hammond #3 of the Virginia Tech Hokies drives against Isaia Howard #23 of the Iowa Hawkeyes during the first half at Tyson Events Center on November 10, 2026 in Sioux City, Iowa. (Photo by Steven Branscombe/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 6-0 Virginia Tech Hokies were back Sunday in the Shriners Children’s Charleston Classic in Charleston, South Carolina. The opponent: the Oklahoma State Cowboys. After a back-and-forth first half with the lead changing often, the Cowboys took control in the second half, outscoring the Hokies 65-39 in the final 20 minutes to win 106-80. Remarkably, this game was tied at halftime. Both teams were hot from the field, with OSU shooting 59% and the Hokies 47% in the first half. Tech made 8-of-15 (53%) from beyond the arc in the first half, while the Cowboys made 5-of-10. While the Hokies cooled off in the second half, Oklahoma State only got hotter. VT made only 11 of 28 field-goal attempts in the second half, including 4-for-14 from the 3-point line, while the Cowboys shot an unheard-of 74% in the second half. And there you have it, that’s the game. The back-and-forth action from the first half carried into the second half. However, back-to-back buckets from Ben Hammond and Amani Hansberry at the 16:31 mark gave the Hokies a 54-51 lead. The crowd sensed the tide might be turning in Virginia Tech’s favor. Instead, it spurred a run by the Cowboys that opened up the game. Oklahoma State scored the next 11 points to build an 8-point lead. The Cowboys never looked back. After a Hammond 3-pointer and two Jaylen Curry free throws cut the lead back to 64-59, OSU scored 13 in a row to blow it wide open. Virginia Tech finishes the weekend 1-1 in Charleston, suffering its first loss of the season. Next up for Virginia Tech is a date with Old Dominion at Cassell Coliseum on Friday. Hammond led the Hokies with 24 points and five rebounds. He was phenomenal as usual, but he had little help. Curry scored 18, but in playing against his former team, he let his emotions get the best of him early, starting down Oklahoma State coach Steve Lutz. Mike Young and Lutz quickly went head-to-head, but it ended as fast as it began, and both coaches laughed it off. Curry led the Hokies with 7 assists, but exhibited poor shot selection at times. Hansberry had a rough game, finishing with 9 points and 6 rebounds and making only 3-of-10 from the field. OSU outrebounded the Hokies 33-27 and Tech had 11 turnovers. Virginia Tech’s continued insistence on living by the 3-point shot can sometimes haunt them. It did on Sunday. Plus, when another team shoots 74% in a half, it’s hard to beat them. The good news is that rarely happens.

sports.title: Greenwich girls swimming holds off Ridgefield for second straight State Open title
sports.description: Greenwich poses for a team photo with their championship plaque and banner after winning the CIAC State Open girls swimming and diving championship on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, at Yale. (Kevin Roberts/Hearst Connecticut Media) NEW HAVEN - The Greenwich girls swimming and diving team captured its second straight State Open title and 23rd overall Sunday by holding off second-place Ridgefield 634-617.5 at Yale. The Cardinals, under first-year head coach Megan Kelly , lost to the Tigers in the regular season before beating them by 18.5 points at FCIACs and 45.5 at Class LL. They completed the trifecta at the Open. "I'm so proud of them," said Kelly, who took over for Brendan Heller, who won four Class LL championships, three State Open titles and three FCIAC championships in five seasons as coach. "Coming in, we knew we had a lot of work to get where we were last year, which was winning the Triple Crown (conference, class and Open titles). It was really tough at the beginning of the season … but they worked really hard in the pool." The Open title was the Cardinals' fourth in the last six years. Ridgefield won crowns in 2022 and 2024. Greenwich senior Kensington Worden led the way with a dramatic victory in the 50 freestyle, touching the wall in 23.57, only .03 seconds ahead of the second-place finisher. For Worden, it was a dream come true. "Coming in as a freshman at this program, it is beyond my wildest dreams ever to become an Open champion," Worden said. "I'm just so happy." Senior Ellison Charette gave Greenwich its second individual title of the meet with a time of 4:57.33 in the 500 freestyle. After that, it was the Cardinals' depth that held off Ridgefield, which had two wins from Zsofia Milak (50.55 in 100 free and 1:50.58 in 200 free) and two from its relays (200 free and 400 free). Ridgefield's 200 free relay of Milak, Dalia Katra, Mary Kelly and Ellen Griffin broke the Open record with a time of 1:34.18. The Tigers held the previous record of 1:35.48, set in 2022. The foursome also won the 400 free relay to end the night. On Thursday, Cardinals sophomore Alden Charette defended her diving crown with a record 561.55 points. The Cardinals' game plan for Sunday was simple. "I told them before this meet, if everyone just moves up one spot individually, we can win," said coach Kelly, a Greenwich alumna and former All-American swimmer. Mission accomplished, but not without months of hard work. "It might seem like it's tiring going two and a half hours every single day, but we are all there and all doing it together, which makes it more special. ... It's full of support and love and everything in between," Worden said. Other individual winners included Norwalk/Brien McMahon's Emma Giafardino in the 200 IM (2:05.05), Weston's McKenzie Parsons in the 100 butterfly (55.54), Wilton's Vedha Kongettira in the 100 backstroke (56.45) and Brookfield's Maggie O'Hara in the 100 breaststroke (1:04.36). (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Notre Dame’s 2026 college football schedule has been called many thing over the last eight months, but “tough” or anywhere near the word “hard” was certainly not among them. Still, some have mentioned that this Irish schedule could look a lot trickier as the season progresses. While they may eventually be true, it may not matter all that much (except for message boards and social media). Notre Dame took a minute or two to get going against the Wisconsin Badgers in the season opener, but eventually the Irish whooped them 42-13. Notre Dame welcomed the Rice Owls to South Bend for the home opener, and sent them back to Texas with a 52-0 loss. Although the Irish were big favorites against Michigan State, they got their best shot — and still beat the Spartans 27-10. The Irish were once again massive favorites over a Big 10 team, and they more than covered against Purdue with a 49-10 win that was never that close. Notre Dame was better than a three touchdown favorite against North Carolina, but ran into a bit of a clunker (and rain) and beat the Tar Heels 37-26. After two weeks on the road, Notre Dame returned to South Bend and the homecooking did them well as the Irish destroyed the Stanford Cardinal 58-7. Disaster hit the Irish against BYU in a 28-24 loss, and no matter what part of the game you want to complain about (because there was quite a bit) the simplest thing to say is that Notre Dame flat out got outplayed by the Cougars. Against Navy, Notre Dame took a slower path than fans would like, but in the end the Irish won the game 35-13 and completely shutdown the Middies in the 2nd half. Notre Dame did “the thing” that fans and pundits have been waiting on, and took down No. 1 Miami in South Bend 31-24. There was no hangover from the massive win over the Canes, and the Irish whipped Boston College at home, 41-7. Notre Dame took care of business against SMU in what was kind of a weird game, but still dominating on many levels. Next up for the Irish is a trip to Syracuse for the final game of the regular season. Notre Dame is still likely to be favored in every game this season, and they are still a popular pick to win the national championship. Their strength of schedule probably isn’t going to matter much, but let’s keep track of it anyway. sports.title: Bam Adebayo Says Heat Are Not Satisfied With 7-Game Win Streak Despite His Triple-Double vs. Thunder
sports.description: MIAMI, FL - NOVEMBER 22: Bam Adebayo #13 of the Miami Heat looks to pass the ball during the game against the Oklahoma City Thunder on November 22, 2026 at Kaseya Center in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Eric Espada/NBAE via Getty Images) Bam Adebayo led the Miami Heat to a comfortable 123-113 win over the severely shorthanded Oklahoma City Thunder tonight. He finished with 24 points, 15 rebounds, 12 assists, two steals, and two blocks, stuffing the box score and recording a triple-double while shooting 8-11 from the field (72.7% FG) to extend the Heat’s winning streak to seven games . After the win, Adebayo spoke to the media and shared his thoughts on his performance and what the seven-game win streak means for the team. “Just making the right reads; obviously, I’ve grown from that point to now. Obviously, I’m more efficient and consistent; that was a fun game to be a part of,” Bam Adebayo said initially about his own performance tonight. Without Giannis Antetokounmpo on the floor tonight, Bam Adebayo played his original center role, where he felt he was much more efficient than at power forward. This performance ties him with LeBron James for the second-most triple-doubles for the Heat (ninth in the regular season), with only Jimmy Butler having recorded more triple-doubles in franchise history (13). But with the team just 16 games into the regular season, Bam Adebayo also said the Heat are not satisfied and should not get complacent, since they had a 3-6 start to the season before the win streak. “We’re not satisfied. I’m glad we won, but we gave up 33 in the fourth quarter. We’re trying to hold teams under 15 made threes, and they made 16. So, I’m satisfied that we’re winning, but I want to win in a way that feels like we’re dominating.” “I want to feel like, when we get out there, there’s a certain physicality and effort. I feel like we show that in sparks and segments, but not for 48 minutes. That’s the goal.” “Obviously, you enjoy winning and being on a streak, but we want to play well not just in the regular season, but deep into the playoffs,” Adebayo concluded . Bam Adebayo’s latest performance showed how effective he can be when given the freedom to operate as the Heat’s primary center. His improved efficiency and playmaking have been key to the Heat’s turnaround, but his comments suggest the team still has plenty of room to grow and no room for complacency. A seven-game winning streak is encouraging, especially after their difficult start, yet Adebayo is focused on building habits that will translate to postseason success. The Heat have improved to 10-6 following tonight’s win. It remains to be seen whether the Heat can become a threatening championship contender in the East after a rocky start to the season, but they finally seem to have steadied their course.

technology.title: $1 of GPT-5.1 tokens finds new ways around China’s Great Firewall
technology.description: Researchers have found new ways to evade China’s Great Firewall after spending just $1 worth of tokens. That result appeared last week in a paper titled “CircumVolve: Automated Discovery of Censorship Evasion Strategies Using Large Language Models” presented at the Conference on Computer and Communications Security run by the Association for Computing Machinery’s Special Interest Group on Security, Audit and Control. Penned by six researchers from the University of Massachusetts Amherst, University of Colorado Boulder, and activist group the Great Firewall Report, the paper points out that finding holes in the Great Firewall is a laborious process – so just the kind of task worth handing to AI. The authors came up with a tool they call “CircumVolve” and describe as “a system for automated discovery of censorship circumvention strategies across the full network stack.” “CircumVolve combines LLM code generation with iterative feedback-driven evaluation to produce verifiable and deployable evasion techniques,” they wrote. “CircumVolve models different censorship techniques as discrete scenarios, each capturing the specific context, protocol constraints, and blocking mechanisms of real-world censors. Within each scenario, evasion strategies are represented as executable Python programs that implement packet and protocol manipulations — from rewriting TCP/IP header fields, to crafting DNS queries that exploit parser ambiguities, to modifying the internal structure of encrypted QUIC Initial packets — while maintaining protocol correctness within tolerable bounds or strategically violating it when beneficial.” The authors tested CircumVolve on simulated censorship tools used by China, Iran, Pakistan, and Kazakhstan, and on virtual private servers deployed on clouds in those countries. Those tests found the median API cost to the first successful evasion was less than $1 in token expenditure costs when using GPT-5.1. The authors acknowledge that operators of censorship infrastructure might be able to observe CircumVolve at work, but feel its relatively small payloads – 80 KB of outgoing and 150 KB of incoming traffic – and 25-45-second pauses between tests might see it fly under the radar. “CircumVolve represents a first step in leveraging LLMs to accelerate the censorship-circumvention lifecycle,” the authors wrote. “By automating the labor-intensive tasks of protocol analysis, implementation, and testing, AI-driven approaches make studying circumvention capabilities far more accessible to the comparatively under-resourced Internet freedom community [and] demonstrates how AI-assisted systems can narrow the resource gap between Internet freedom advocates and well-funded censoring states.” Lenovo finally cracks monster datacenter profits Ever since acquiring IBM’s x86 server business in 2014, Chinese hardware giant Lenovo has struggled to turn a profit from datacenter sales, even as it expanded its business into storage, networking, and selling to hypersc

science.title: Watch live on Nov. 23: Amazon launching 1st batch of internet satellites since Vulcan Centaur failure
science.description: null Another batch of Amazon internet satellites will fly on Monday morning (Nov. 23), just eight days after a launch failure doomed 40 of the spacecraft. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation is scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana on Monday, during a 29-minute window that opens at 6:09 a.m. EST (1109 GMT; 8:09 a.m. local time in Kourou). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of Arianespace, the French company that operates the Ariane 6. Coverage will begin about 30 minutes before launch. An Ariane 6 rocket launches 32 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit from French Guiana on Feb. 12, 2026. (Image credit: ESA/CNES/Arianespace-ArianeGroup/Optique Video du CSG-P. Piron) Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit , will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft. Amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur , suffered a problem shortly after launch. Ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' company has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's New Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9 . Vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And New Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test. The Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure. Monday's mission will be the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year.

science.title: 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson
science.description: 7 Min Read 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano, former NASA astronaut Russell “Rusty” Schweickart, and NASA astronauts Frank Rubio and Bob Hines appear onstage at the Artemis Celebration Gala at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Merritt Island, Florida, on Nov. 6, 2026. Credits: Purpose Entertainment/Shanna Lockwood Employees and guests of NASA’s Johnson Space Center celebrate the center’s 65th anniversary at the Lunar Receiving Park in Houston on Nov. 19, 2026. NASA/Robert Markowitz For 65 years, NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston has helped shape human spaceflight, from the Gemini missions that demonstrated rendezvous and docking techniques needed for Apollo to the research conducted aboard the International Space Station, which has supported a continuous human presence for more than 26 years. Today, Johnson teams are preparing crews and systems for NASA’s next chapter: returning astronauts to the lunar surface and building the capabilities needed for a long-term human presence at the Moon. Across those missions, generations of flight controllers, engineers, scientists, instructors, medical specialists, and other experts have helped crews live and work beyond Earth. Johnson is home to NASA’s Orion and Moon Base programs, and its teams continue to support space station operations, astronaut training, spacecraft development, mission operations, and human health. Mercury and Gemini: Preparing for Apollo When the Manned Spacecraft Center officially opened on Nov. 1, 1961, NASA had already flown two suborbital Mercury missions, with the first orbital flight just months away. Most Project Mercury activities remained at Cape Canaveral in Florida to maintain continuity, but the new Project Gemini took up residence in Houston, housed in temporary leased facilities across the city while construction of the new Clear Lake campus continued. The new Mission Control Center became NASA’s primary flight control center in June 1965, with the Gemini IV mission that included the first American spacewalk. Houston became the nerve center for American human spaceflight, overseeing the remaining eight Gemini missions before transitioning to the Apollo program. Following the tragic Apollo 1 fire in January 1967, managers, engineers, and astronauts at the Manned Spacecraft Center applied lessons learned to make the spacecraft safer and ensure the safety of its astronauts, resuming crewed missions in October 1968. Managers in Houston devised a daring plan to send Apollo 8 on a circumlunar flight. In December 1968, Apollo 8 made its historic trip around the Moon, and seven months later Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin “Buzz” Aldrin landed on the lunar surface. Their first voice transmission back to Earth after their arrival began with the word “Houston.” Five more Moon landings completed the Apollo program and humanity’s first phase of lunar exploration

A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base 's Launch Complex-4E on Sunday (Nov. 22) at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California), on a mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) called NROL-136. It was the second launch from that pad in a little over 32 hours, after the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force . And that quick turnaround made history. Massive high five to the @SpaceX west coast team for a world record launch to launch turn from Pad 4e last night! 32 hr, 3 min, 21 sec! This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin. This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin. Next goal… the 24 hr turn!" Kiko Dontchev, SpaceX's vice president of launch, said via X on Sunday . (Pad 40 is at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.) NROL-136 was the sixth launch of 2026 so far for the NRO. All of them have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9, and all have delivered classified satellites to low Earth orbit . The launch marked another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. About two minutes after liftoff, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued carrying the classified payloads onward to orbit. The booster then reversed course and returned to Vandenberg, touching down at Landing Zone 4 approximately seven and a half minutes after launch. Saturday's launch was the 14th flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster, dubbed B1097, which previously launched NASA 's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 for the Space Force, and eight Starlink missions. NROL-136 was the 15th launch dedicated to building the NRO's "proliferated architecture," the satellites for which have been developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space , according to the NRO's mission website . science.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
science.description: null On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together. science.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
science.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part. The moon will arrive exactly on schedule — that's guaranteed. Everything else — the weather, the crowds, the transport, the equipment and the people — is rather less predictable. From the possibility of dust storms to uncertainty about whether boats will even be allowed to move on the Nile, there are plenty of reasons to be slightly wary about what awaits eclipse chasers after the ultimate bragging rights on Aug. 2, 2027. Here are the 10 things worrying me most about the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt. A dust storm could make the eclipsed sun less impressive. (Image credit: Grant Faint via Getty Images) 1. A sudden dust storm The chances of cloud-free skies in Luxor and anywhere in Upper Egypt in August are exceptionally high — close to 100%. That's almost unheard of in eclipse-chasing. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. Although the sun will almost certainly be visible during the eclipse, airborne dust could hide the delicate structure of the solar corona. 2. Chaos in Luxor How many people will descend on Luxor for the eclipse? August is normally a quiet month for tourism in Luxor because of the oppressive heat. In 2027, however, the city and its surrounding urban area — population about four million — could swell as eclipse chasers, tour groups, photographers and curious visitors descend. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). She points out that his Moby-Dick-esque obsession is on the verge of going full Ahab, and he eventually sees sense, issuing the order to abandon the Enterprise and destroy the hive. It's a masterclass showcasing the ever-brilliant Stewart's impressive range, as the out-of-control captain's rarely seen temper reaches fever pitch, before normal service is resumed. science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. science.description: null Update for 2 p.m. ET on Nov. 22: On Sunday afternoon (Nov. 22), the BepiColombo team announced that, while the spacecraft did successfully arrive in orbit around Mercury on Saturday (Nov. 21), things didn't go entirely according to plan. "During the manoeuvre, the thruster burn was shorter than planned due to a software issue," the mission team said via X . "The spacecraft is safe & teams at ESOC are working to understand what happened. Updates provided on Monday." For just the second time ever, Mercury has received a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — arrived in orbit around Mercury on Saturday (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. Before BepiColombo, just one spacecraft had ever circled the solar system's innermost planet: NASA's MESSENGER , which did so from March 2011 to April 2015. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must therefore shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Saturday's orbital insertion came after a 37-minute-long engine burn, which began at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT). There was a bit drama involved, however, as confirmation of the maneuver's success didn't come for several hours afterward. "We've heard back from Bepi — the spacecraft is now in contact with the ground and the teams at ESOC [the European Space Operations Centre] are busy assessing the telemetry. science.description: null SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Nov. 20, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit. USSF-317 is a classified mission, so we don't know what the upper stage is carrying or where exactly it's headed. (Image credit: SpaceX) Previous Booster 1100 missions NROL-105 | USSF-385 | 8 Starlink missions USSF-317 was the 121st Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the third mission that SpaceX has launched for the Space Force so far in November. The vast majority of this year's Falcon 9 missions — about 70% of them — have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink LEO internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 satellites. The Falcon 9 has been putting up incredible numbers lately — it flew a whopping 165 times in 2025 , for example — but the workhorse rocket is on its way out . science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers.
